summary: Upgraded the ClientApp from Angular 12.2 to Angular 13.4 with `ng update @angular/core@13 @angular/cli@13`, which ran all v13 migrations (IE polyfill removal, angular.json cleanup including the removed tslint builder, empty `[routerLink]` fix, TestBed teardown opt-out) and moved TypeScript to 4.6.4; NgRx was bumped 12.5 -> 13.2 to match. The two breaking changes that needed hand work were webpack 5's loss of automatic Node core-module polyfills (the browser entry re-exported `@angular/platform-server`, which now fails to resolve 'url') and npm 8's strict peer resolution, which rejected the Angular 7-era `@nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader` and the jasmine-core/karma-jasmine-html-reporter pair. A clean `npm install`, `npm run build` and `npm run build:ssr` all pass on Node 16; `npm test` still fails with the identical pre-existing angular.json misconfiguration it failed with at baseline.
changes: Ran `npx -p @angular/cli@13 ng update @angular/core@13 @angular/cli@13 --allow-dirty --force`; all v13 migrations executed.
src/polyfills.ts: the migration removed the IE-only polyfill block (IE 11 support was dropped in v13).
angular.json: the migration removed the two `lint` targets, because the `@angular-devkit/build-angular:tslint` builder no longer exists in v13, and dropped other options no longer valid in v13.
.gitignore: `/.angular/cache` added for the new persistent build cache.

src/app/fetch-employee/fetch-employee.component.html: `[routerLink]=""` -> `[routerLink]="[]"`; in v13 an empty/undefined routerLink disables the link instead of routing to the current page, so the Delete anchor needed the explicit empty-commands form to keep behaving as before.
src/test.ts: the migration added `teardown: { destroyAfterEach: false }` to `initTestEnvironment`, opting the existing suite out of v13's new default TestBed teardown.

Split the SSR entry point out of the browser entry: the re-export `export { renderModule, renderModuleFactory } from '@angular/platform-server'` moved from src/main.ts into a new src/main.server.ts, and the `server` target's `main` plus tsconfig.server.json's `files` now point at it. Under webpack 5 the browser build no longer auto-polyfills Node core modules, so bundling platform-server into the browser entry failed with `Can't resolve 'url'`. The export was dead weight in the browser bundle anyway; the server bundle still emits the same `dist-server/main.<hash>.js` exporting renderModule/renderModuleFactory, so the ASP.NET prerendering contract is unchanged.

src/tsconfig.server.json: added `"types": []` (mirroring tsconfig.app.json). Without it the server build pulled in every @types package in node_modules and failed to typecheck against @types/jasmine and @types/ws.

Removed @nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader (pinned at 7.1.0) from package.json and dropped `ModuleMapLoaderModule` from src/app/app.server.module.ts. Its Angular ^7.1.4 peers made `npm install` fail outright under npm 8's strict peer resolution, and with Ivy the module is a no-op, so removing it is behaviour-preserving.

Bumped jasmine-core ~3.6 -> ~3.10 and @types/jasmine ~3.6 -> ~3.10 (the versions Angular 13 scaffolds): karma-jasmine-html-reporter 1.7 peer-requires jasmine-core >= 3.8, which also blocked a strict `npm install`.
Ran `ng update @ngrx/store@13`, moving all five @ngrx packages 12.5.1 -> 13.2.0; the v13 NgRx migrations found nothing to change in the source.
TypeScript moved 4.3.5 -> 4.6.4 by the CLI update; no source changes were needed.

package-lock.json regenerated through npm; verified with `rm -rf node_modules && npm install` with default (strict) peer resolution, exit 0, followed by passing `npm run build` and `npm run build:ssr`.
manual_followups: `npm test` fails at baseline and still fails with the identical cause: the karma target in angular.json lists `"styles": ["styles.css"]` instead of `"src/styles.css"`, so the builder cannot resolve the entry (ENOENT on ClientApp/styles.css). Pre-existing, not a regression, but it means the suite has never actually run and the v13 TestBed-teardown opt-out in src/test.ts is unverified.

`npm run lint` is now broken: the v13 CLI migration deleted both `lint` targets from angular.json because the tslint builder was removed in v13. tslint and codelyzer are still listed in optionalDependencies and should be replaced with @angular-eslint, or the `lint` script dropped.
The TestBed teardown opt-out (`destroyAfterEach: false`) added by the migration is a compatibility shim. Once the test target is fixed, remove it and let the suite run with v13's default teardown.

Now that the browser and server entry points are separate files, `src/main.server.ts` only re-exports platform-server; a person may want to move to the modern @nguniversal/express-engine layout, which is the supported SSR path from here on.
src/tsconfig.server.json now sets `"types": []`. If server-side code later needs Node globals, add `"node"` back explicitly rather than reverting to the implicit all-@types behaviour.
node-sass 4.x (an optionalDependency) still fails to build on this image and is skipped. Nothing uses Sass, so it blocks nothing, but it should be removed or replaced with `sass`.
The build still warns that @angular/platform-server depends on 'domino' (CommonJS optimization bailout) in the server bundle. Harmless; silenceable via `allowedCommonJsDependencies`.
`"defaultConfiguration": ""` is still set on the build and server targets (inherited from the v12 hop). Schema-valid and behaviour-preserving, but worth setting deliberately.
core-js 2.6.5 is still a dependency and is unmaintained; nothing imports it since the polyfills cleanup, so it is likely removable.
